body:
## Graph and Partition Indexes Take Different Shortcuts

One index links each vector to promising neighbors; another divides space into regions and searches only selected regions. Both avoid a full scan differently.

Graph indexes often give strong recall with memory-heavy links. Partitioned indexes can compress vectors and suit larger collections, but require careful training and probing.

Benchmark with production-sized data and concurrency. Cache behavior, filtered searches, write rate, and tail latency can matter more than a single-query average.
common_mistakes: A vector database removes the need to store source text.
Approximate search is guaranteed to return the exact same neighbors.
Access control should be applied only after private text reaches the model.
mini_exercise: Draw “Graph and Partition Indexes Take Different Shortcuts” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Large retrieval systems need fast similarity search plus filters, updates, metadata, and operational guarantees.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Graph and Partition Indexes Take Different Shortcuts,” explain Vector Databases without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
